statements.name: PROC HYPERTUNE
statements.description: The PROC HYPERTUNE statement invokes the procedure and specifies global options that control the algorithm, execution limits, convergence, evaluation cache, input and output data sets, and logging.

arguments.name: ALGORITHM=
arguments.description: specifies the optimization algorithm.

arguments.name: ABSFCONV=
arguments.description: specifies the absolute function convergence criterion. The procedure stops when the improvement in the best objective value between successive iterations falls below the specified value.

arguments.name: FEASTOL=
arguments.description: specifies the feasibility tolerance for constraints. A point whose constraint violation does not exceed the specified value is treated as feasible.

arguments.name: NABSFCONV=
arguments.description: specifies the number of consecutive iterations without improvement that are required before the procedure declares convergence and terminates.

arguments.name: MAXFUNC=
arguments.description: specifies the number of objective function evaluations.

arguments.name: MAXITER=
arguments.description: specifies the maximum number of iterations. For population-based algorithms, this is the number of generations.

arguments.name: MAXTIME=
arguments.description: specifies the maximum time (in seconds) that the procedure runs.

arguments.name: NPARALLEL=
arguments.description: specifies the number of objective evaluations to perform in parallel.

arguments.name: SEED=
arguments.description: specifies the pseudorandom number seed, which controls the reproducibility of stochastic algorithms.

arguments.name: NGLOBAL=
arguments.description: specifies the number of global searches.

arguments.name: NLOCAL=
arguments.description: specifies the number of local searches.

arguments.name: PARETOMAX=
arguments.description: specifies the maximum number of Pareto-optimal points to retain.

arguments.name: POPSIZE=
arguments.description: specifies the population size for population-based algorithms.

arguments.name: CACHEIN=
arguments.description: names an input data set of previously computed evaluations. Points in this data set are loaded into the cache before the search begins, which warm-starts the run.

arguments.name: CACHEOUT=
arguments.description: names an output data set that receives the full evaluation cache: every distinct point that is evaluated, together with its objective values, constraint values, and feasibility status.

arguments.name: CACHETOL=
arguments.description: specifies the tolerance that is used to determine whether a candidate point matches a point already in the cache. The value must be nonnegative.

arguments.name: CACHEMAX=
arguments.description: specifies the maximum number of entries that the cache retains.

arguments.name: FIRSTGEN=
arguments.description: names an input data set of starting points for the search.

arguments.name: LASTGEN=
arguments.description: names an output data set of the points in the final iteration.

arguments.name: PRIMALIN=
arguments.description: names an input data set of initial solutions.

arguments.name: PRIMALOUT=
arguments.description: names the output data set of the best solution(s) that is found.

arguments.name: LOGFREQ=
arguments.description: specifies that the procedure print an iteration log line every nn iterations.

arguments.name: LOGLEVEL=
arguments.description: specifies the amount of information to write to the SAS log. Specify LOGLEVEL=0 to suppress log messages or LOGLEVEL=1 for the standard log.

arguments.name: PRINTLEVEL=
arguments.description: specifies the amount of ODS output. Specify PRINTLEVEL=0 to suppress the ODS tables or PRINTLEVEL=1 to create the summary tables.

statements.name: CON
statements.description: The CON statement declares one nonlinear constraint. Specify one CON statement for each nonlinear constraint. The constraint name must match the name of a SAS macro in the SUBMIT block that computes the constraint value. Nonlinear constraint functions are evaluated together with the objective functions during each evaluation.

arguments.name: LB=
arguments.description: specifies the lower bound on the constraint value.

arguments.name: UB=
arguments.description: specifies the upper bound on the constraint value.

statements.name: LINCON
statements.description: The LINCON statement specifies a SAS data set that defines linear constraints. Use this statement for algebraic linear constraints that can be supplied as data rather than computed in the SUBMIT block.

statements.name: OBJ
statements.description: The OBJ statement declares one objective function. Specify one OBJ statement for each objective; specifying more than one objective produces a multiobjective (Pareto) problem. The objective name must match the name of a SAS macro that is defined in the SUBMIT block.

arguments.name: TYPE=
arguments.description: specifies whether to minimize or maximize the objective.

statements.name: SUBMIT
statements.description: The SUBMIT block contains the SAS macro code that evaluates the objectives and nonlinear constraints. The code runs once per candidate solution: PROC HYPERTUNE passes the decision variable values in and reads the objective and constraint values out.

statements.name: VAR
statements.description: The VAR statement declares one decision variable. Specify one VAR statement for each variable in the problem. The specified variable name must match a parameter name of the objective function in the SUBMIT block.

arguments.name: LB=
arguments.description: specifies the lower bound of the variable.

arguments.name: UB=
arguments.description: specifies the upper bound of the variable.

arguments.name: INIT=
arguments.description: specifies the initial value of the variable.

arguments.name: TYPE=
arguments.description: specifies the variable type.

arguments.name: SCALE=
arguments.description: specifies how to scale the variable during the search.

arguments.name: SCALEFACTOR=
arguments.description: specifies the scaling factor to use when SCALE=FACTOR.
